questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Actions speak louder than words
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Actions speak louder than words

options.text: What you do reveals the real you
options.html: What you do reveals the real you

options.text: What you do is your own business
options.html: What you do is your own business

options.text: What you can see may not be true
options.html: What you can see may not be true

options.text: What you don’t say is what you are
options.html: What you don’t say is what you are

questions.solution:
The correct answer is - What you do reveals the real you.

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given proverb:
    • Actions speak louder than words​ - what someone actually does means more than what they say they will do.
  • Example: 
    • They are not expected to win, but they believe actions speak louder than words.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In a fog
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

In a fog
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Confused and dazed'.

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: In a fog means in great confusion.
    • Example: He went through the day with his mind in a fog.
  • From the given options, the third option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "In a fog" that it is all about trapped in foggy weather, but the correct answer is option 3. So be careful while dealing with such questions.
     

Additional Information

  • Although the origin of this idiom is not available. Contextually, ''in a fog" is used in situations where we are not attentive to what is happening and seem to be like in the actual fog whose literal meaning is smoky like surroundings. Although these expressions “in a fog” and “in a haze” allude to obscuring one’s view. The term ‘fog’ usage dates from about the 1600s, ‘haze’ from the mid-1800s.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Falling head over heels
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Falling head over heels

options.text: Falling deeply in love with someone
options.html: Falling deeply in love with someone

options.text: feeling deep sympathy to the needy
options.html: feeling deep sympathy to the needy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Falling deeply in love with someone'. 

Key Points

  • The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom 'Falling head over heels' is 'Falling deeply in love with someone'. 
  • Falling head over heels: If you fall head over heels or fall head over heels in love, you fall suddenly and deeply in love with someone
    • Example: You have to remember that I was head over heels in love with Bill.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: Falling deeply in love with someone. 

Additional Information

  • Let's look at some idioms:
    • Idiom Meaning Example
      A piece of the action a part of the profits or advantages that come from an activity When it comes to lawsuits, everyone seems to want a piece of the action.
      A piece of the pie a share of something When the business started making money, everyone in his family wanted a piece of the pie.
      A piece of the action involvement in something successful that someone else has started Now research has proved that the drug is effective, everyone wants a piece of the action.

  • दिए गए मुहावरे का सबसे उपयुक्त अर्थ है, 'किसी के साथ प्यार में पड़ना'।
  • Falling head over heels:- यदि आप ऊँची एड़ी के जूते पर सिर झुकाते हैं या प्यार में ऊँची एड़ी के जूते पर गिरते हैं, तो आप किसी के साथ प्यार में अचानक और गहराई से गिरते हैं ।
    • उदाहरण: You have to remember that I was head over heels in love with Bill.
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।
    उन्होंने कहा कि इस तरह की घटनाओं को रोकने के लिए सरकार की ओर से कोई ठोस कदम नहीं उठाया गया है।

सही वाक्य: Falling deeply in love with someone. 

Additional Information

  • आइए कुछ मुहावरों को देखें:
    • मुहावरा जिसका अर्थ है उदाहरण
      A piece of the action मुनाफे या फायदे का एक हिस्सा जो एक गतिविधि से आता है When it comes to lawsuits, everyone seems to want a piece of the action
      A piece of the pie किसी चीज़ का हिस्सा
      When the business started making money, everyone in his family wanted a piece of the pie.

       
      A piece of the action किसी और चीज में सफल होना जो किसी और ने शुरू किया हो Now research has proved that the drug is effective, everyone wants a piece of the action.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cut to the chase
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Cut to the chase

options.text: Stopping unexpectedly and missing the chase
options.html: Stopping unexpectedly and missing the chase

options.text: Talking about the important point and leaving out the detail
options.html: Talking about the important point and leaving out the detail

options.text: Cutting long pieces and spoiling the dish cooked
options.html: Cutting long pieces and spoiling the dish cooked

options.text: Sleeping long hours and spoiling the health
options.html: Sleeping long hours and spoiling the health

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Talking about the important point and leaving out the detail'.

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Cut to the chase means to leave out all unnecessary details and deal with the major points.
    • Example: In business meetings, Richardson likes to cut to the chase.
  • From the given options, the second option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is Talking about the important point and leaving out the detail.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Cut to the chase" that it is all about something related to chasing anything, but the correct answer is option 2. So be careful while dealing with such questions.
     

Additional Information

  • This phrase originated in the US film industry. Many silent films used to have a romantic storyline that climaxed in a chase sequence. The phrase was used in a literal sense in directing films around the 1920s. In the figurative or idiomatic was, it was used since the 1940s.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom. Back in saddle
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom.

Back in saddle
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Resume duty.

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given idiom:
    • Back in the saddle- doing something that you stopped doing for a period of time
  • Example: 
    •  I needed to take a break for a bit, but now, I'm back in the saddle.
  • ​Thus from the explanation given above, we find that the 1st option is the correct choice.
     

 ​​​​Additional Information  

  • Let's look at the origin of the idiom:

    • The expression 'get back in the saddle' came into use in the 1800s. The image is of someone, such as a jockey or cowboy, who has fallen off a horse and must get back in the saddle to resume riding the horse. Common wisdom dictates that someone who falls off a horse must immediately return to the saddle in order to conquer the horse’s temperament and one’s fears.

questions.question: Directions: Each of the following questions has underlined idioms/phrases. Each sentence is followed by four options. Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase. His guide asked him to pull up his socks if he wanted a good rank.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Each of the following questions has underlined idioms/phrases. Each sentence is followed by four options. Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase.

His guide asked him to pull up his socks if he wanted a good rank.

options.text: make a greater effort to improve
options.html: make a greater effort to improve

options.text: give attention to his appearance also
options.html: give attention to his appearance also

options.text: take care to be more formal
options.html: take care to be more formal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 (make a greater effort to improve).

Key Points

  • The phrase "pull up your socks" means to make a greater effort to improve or to get ready to perform better. (अपने प्रदर्शन को बेहतर बनाने के लिए अधिक प्रयास करना)
    • Example: If he wants to pass this semester, he’ll need to pull up his socks and start studying seriously.
  • Explanation of the correct phrase: The idiom "pull up your socks" is often used to encourage someone to work harder or prepare themselves to face challenges. (इस वाक्यांश का उपयोग किसी को अधिक मेहनत करने या चुनौतियों का सामना करने के लिए तैयार होने के लिए प्रेरित करने के लिए किया जाता है।)
    • Example: The coach asked the team to pull up their socks if they wanted to win the tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (make a greater effort to improve).

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 2: give attention to his appearance also (अपने रूप-रंग पर भी ध्यान देना):
    • Example: He decided to give more attention to his appearance before attending the formal dinner.
  • Option 3: take care to be more formal (अधिक औपचारिक होने का ध्यान रखना):
    • Example: The new employee was advised to take care to be more formal in his emails.
  • Option 4: dress more carefully and neatly (अधिक सावधानी और साफ-सुथरे तरीके से कपड़े पहनना):
    • Example: The teacher advised the students to dress more carefully and neatly for the school event.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiomatic expression given. At a stone’s throw
